\usepackage{fuzz}
\begin{document}

\section{A violation that truncation hides}

This specification settles a question no argument could: can an incomplete
model check report ``no counter example found'' on a specification that has
one?

\texttt{Step} leads from the initial state to $maxFan$ \emph{distinct}
successors --- one per value of $choice?$ --- and exactly one of them,
$pos = maxFan$, has nothing enabled. It is a deadlock, and no other path
reaches it.

The distinctness is the point. \texttt{MAX\_OPERATIONS} bounds the transitions
computed per operation, and transitions sharing a successor collapse, so a
trap behind a \emph{shared} successor is found however hard the run is
truncated. A trap behind its own successor is not: cut the transition and the
state is never visited, never checked, and never reported.

Run it twice:

\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{-p MAX\_OPERATIONS 2000} --- the deadlock is found.
  \item \texttt{-p MAX\_OPERATIONS 3} --- ``No counter example found. However,
    not all transitions were computed !'', \texttt{deadlocked:0},
    \texttt{ALL OPERATIONS COVERED}, and exit status 0.
\end{itemize}

\begin{zed}
  maxFan == 1000
\end{zed}

\begin{schema}{Probe}
  pos : \nat
\where
  pos \leq maxFan
\end{schema}

\begin{schema}{InitProbe}
  Probe'
\where
  pos' = 0
\end{schema}

\begin{schema}{Step}
  \Delta Probe \\
  choice? : \nat
\where
  pos = 0 \\
  choice? \geq 1 \\
  choice? \leq maxFan \\
  pos' = choice?
\end{schema}

\begin{schema}{Hold}
  \Delta Probe
\where
  pos \geq 1 \\
  pos < maxFan \\
  pos' = pos
\end{schema}
